title: Playing with George Lewis, Sonny Henry and Al Morgan
summary: French recalls Lewis, Sonny Henry the trombonist and bassist Al Morgan, all linked to Rena's band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Did you ever work with George Lewis? George Lewis? Mm-hmm.
Yes. What band would that be?
George Lewis. Mm-hmm. Oh, he was a long time.
George Lewis was a player with Rainy, too.
Was he in there before Zab or after?
I don't know. I can't think it's been so long.
I don't know when I was. I used to play with George Ritz a lot of times. That's what got me. I can't get away from me.
I guess they just swapped around so much.
I played with George Ritz a lot. I played in the band with Sonny Henry and all them different things. We rode it across the river.
He passed too, Sonny Henry. Yeah, he did. January. We were at his funeral. Sonny Henry was with what band?
Sonny Henry, you worked with him?

Sonny Henry used to play with him. You get a Sammo? Yeah. Yeah. Trombones. Then he got that, what that other fella? Jim Crow. Yeah. And Jim Crow started playing with him. Oh, that's a guy that can teach me Jim Crow. But Sonny Henry is better trombone playing than Jim Crow. Yeah.
Sonny Henry. Sonny Henry is a good trombone playing.

When we made that big show here in town there, you remember? Uh-huh. Boy, he had him a big bottle like that. Yeah. He said, man, he said, I want to get up there and blow something. They ain't playing nothing. Let me blow something.
Did you ever work with Al Morgan? You remember him? His bass player?
Albert Morgan? Uh-huh. Yes, sir. We had him playing with us, sir. You played with Rainey, too. Oh, yeah. He played a long time with Rainey.
